content.overview: Section 2 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 defines key terms used throughout the Act, including environment, environmental pollutant, environmental pollution, handling, hazardous substance, occupier and related expressions. Correct application of later operative sections (ss. 3, 7, 8, 15 and others) depends on these definitions. Always read the definition against the official text as in force.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Which defined term is in issue? (2) Does the factual medium match the statutory definition? (3) How does the definition feed ss. 3/7/8/15 analysis?
content.study:
Definitions control the scope of duties and penalties. Do not expand environment or hazardous substance beyond the enacted meaning without the text.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Function of s. 2
sections.body: Supplies statutory meanings for environment, pollutant, pollution, handling, hazardous substance, occupier and other defined terms used in the Act.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.body: Includes water, air and land and the inter-relationship which exists among and between water, air and land, and human beings, other living creatures, plants, micro-organism and property — as defined.

sections.heading: Environmental pollutant / pollution
sections.body: Any solid, liquid or gaseous substance present in such concentration as may be, or tend to be, injurious to environment; pollution is the presence of any environmental pollutant.

sections.heading: Hazardous substance and handling
sections.body: Substance which by reason of chemical or physico-chemical properties or handling is liable to cause harm; handling includes manufacture, processing, treatment, package, storage, transportation, use, collection, destruction, conversion, offering for sale, transfer — as defined.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify the term; quote the definition; apply to facts before invoking operative sections.

examples.title: Pollutant question
examples.body: Whether a discharged substance is an environmental pollutant under s. 2 turns on concentration and injurious tendency as defined — then ss. 7 and 15 analysis follows.

hypotheticals.question: Can s. 7 be applied without checking s. 2 definitions?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Whether a substance is an environmental pollutant and whether an activity is handling a hazardous substance depends on s. 2.

distinctions.title: s. 2 definitions vs s. 3 powers
distinctions.left: Defines terms used in the Act.
distinctions.right: Empowers Central Government to take measures and issue directions/rules.

misconceptions.trap: s. 2 is only dictionary material and can be ignored in answers.
misconceptions.correction: Operative duties and penalties are controlled by these definitions; exam answers should state the relevant definition.
